answer: Each agent may create a new identity, but earning influence requires locking scarce tokens in a public bond that other participants can slash after proving the agent double-signed or broke a protocol rule. A fake identity therefore adds no weight for free: to capture a larger share of votes, an attacker must split capital across more bonds, keep it locked during the challenge period, and risk losing it. An ember account entering through an inlet still faces the same bond; the delta is measurable capital at risk per added identity.
